aboutYourselfAndWhyAtomicSemi: I am completing an M.S. in Robotics and Autonomous Systems with an AI concentration at Arizona State University after earning a B.S. in Computer Science. I enjoy engineering where perception, controls, software, and physical hardware meet. My graduate projects include camera-LiDAR perception and localization, real-time control and sensor fusion on a Parrot MiniDrone, and ROS/Gazebo motion planning. I am drawn to Atomic Semi because the Tool Software team owns problems end to end, from computer vision and state estimation to motion control, calibration, simulation, and hardware debugging. That breadth matches how I like to work: follow the evidence across domains, test carefully, and turn an algorithm into reliable behavior on a physical system.
projectYouAreMostProudOf:
I am most proud of optimizing a TransFuser camera-LiDAR perception system for autonomous robotics. My goal was to reduce model complexity without sacrificing the multi-task outputs needed for localization, navigation, depth estimation, detection, segmentation, and BEV mapping. I replaced the original backbone with EfficientNetV2-S and adapted the multi-scale transformer fusion and training pipeline around it. This reduced the model from 168 million to 50 million parameters, a 70% reduction, while improving held-out loss by 8.7%. The resulting system also improved BEV segmentation by 25.4%.

I owned the model integration, data-loading and training workflow, evaluation setup, and failure analysis. During mixed-precision training, I traced a critical instability to CenterNet focal loss under FP16, tested the hypothesis, and implemented a stable correction rather than masking the symptom. The project strengthened my ability to connect model architecture, numerical behavior, evaluation metrics, and real robotics outputs. It also taught me that optimization is valuable only when the complete system remains measurable and reliable.
